title: Bryant Jackson reflects on service and leadership at University of South Dakota
text:
Bryant Jackson reflects on service and leadership at University of South Dakota
Bryant Jackson, chief of police at the University of South Dakota, shared on July 8 his journey from Yankton High School to leading campus safety efforts at USD. Jackson recalled early connections to the university, including friends who attended USD and memories of the 2005 high school football championship in the DakotaDome.
Jackson began his official tenure with USD in 2015 after serving in the United States Marine Corps and completing both bachelor’s and master’s degrees. He said, “The most rewarding aspect about working at USD is being surrounded by individuals who strive to better themselves and their profession daily.”
Inspired by colleagues and motivated by the academic environment, Jackson enrolled in USD’s Doctor of Education program focused on adult and higher education. He said this decision strengthened his leadership skills and deepened his commitment to supporting students, faculty, and staff. “Our students are here to learn and grow. Our faculty members provide expert instruction and advance their fields through research and advocacy. This type of energy is contagious. I am driven daily by their example to strive to do better in all aspects of life and my professional obligations,” he said.
Since becoming chief of police in 2021, Jackson has worked to maintain a safe campus environment while also contributing nationally as a member of the International Association of Chiefs of Police’s Police Investigative Operations Committee and as first vice president for the International Association of Campus Law Enforcement Administrators. “It is truly a privilege to work at USD and serve this community,” Jackson said. “Every day brings the opportunity to support our students, collaborate with dedicated faculty and staff, and contribute to a campus environment where people feel safe, supported and able to grow.”
Jackson remains modest about his contributions but emphasizes gratitude for being part of an institution committed to its mission: “Being part of a place that is so committed to its people and its mission is something I never take for granted,” he said.
USD also supports student engagement through programs such as those offered by its Department of Sustainability and Environment, which promotes cultural well-being through action on campus or along the Missouri River; uses facilities like Akeley-Lawrence Science Center; functions within the College of Arts & Sciences; inspires positive change; offers unique undergraduate/graduate degrees in sustainability; and extends influence via partnerships like Missouri River Institute along Missouri National Recreational River—all according to the official website.
